study_type: exploratory follow-up; these people and associations were inspected previously
question: Do gait-derived features reduce held-out POMA prediction error beyond a flexible speed-only baseline?
clinical_target: Recorded POMA total 0..28, NOT TUG/SPPB, NOT fall outcomes
evaluation: 25 leave-one-person-out outer fits; 4 seeded person-fold inner fits for penalty and speed degree; seed 20261103
functional_training: Only the other 24 eligible older stroke people; no fabricated healthy POMA
inputs: Exactly previous accepted primary side_pan, zero toe offset, 124 frames at 30 Hz; same windows for every feature comparison; window mean then equal trial mean then person
speed: Verified original session mean speed, both sides averaged; not a camera-measured speed; same speed for every arm

arms.C_predicted_deviation: speed + separately fitted 2D-to-own-deviation estimate using age65plus healthy reference
arms.D_joint2D: speed + 2D joint position, knee angle, asymmetry and short-window periodicity descriptors
arms.E_joint3D: diagnostic: speed + 3D descriptors for exactly same joints and frames
arms.F_measured_deviation: diagnostic: speed + measured session 3D angular deviation; session summary is not restricted to 124-frame windows
arms.C_allhealthy: secondary C using all healthy reference

upstream_deviation: Completely exclude all 25 primary people from upstream training and hyperparameter selection. 33 remaining matched-input people are auxiliary. Healthy reference uses linked 40 age65+ curves, or all138 secondary; leave normal individual out of own target; exclude upstream validation people from reference during tuning. 3 person folds stratified by cohort, ridge alpha [.1,1,10,100,1000]. This is a newly rebuilt matched-window model, not reuse of previous OOF estimates.
summary_features: C: 8 existing toe-free channels per leg, mean/SD/p05/p25/p50/p75/p95/derivativeRMS=128. D/E: common hip/knee/ankle normalized by mean thigh length centered at hip midpoint, Gaussian sigma1; per leg coordinates + knee angle + bilateral ankle forward difference; same 8 stats; bilateral mean and absolute side difference. Knee autocorrelation peak over lags15..90, period and peak strength each summarized across sides; bilateral knee correlation. No clinical cadence, contact phase, or long-term variability claim.
functional_model: Standardized ridge with separate fixed unit-total squared-scale feature blocks (speed and added features); speed polynomial degree1/2/3 and alpha [.01,.1,1,10,100] chosen by pooled inner MAE; prediction clipped to 0..28 before selection/evaluation. Constant median training target secondary baseline.
selection: No outcome-dependent exclusion or feature screening; no alternate model search after seeing results
primary_metric: person MAE and paired difference versus A; lower is better
uncertainty: 10000 paired person bootstraps seed20261103 on fixed outer predictions, conditional not full retraining; 95% intervals all; primary B/C/D also 98.333% intervals for three comparisons; descriptive only on this exploratory sample
subgroups: POMA 0..18,19..24,25..28 descriptive score bins, not validated risk categories; MAE, bias, max, fraction error>5, within2; lowest bin missed when predicted>18, and false alarms in others
controls: 5 fixed auxiliary-feature permutation seeds 20261113..20261117 for D_joint2D, preserving person speed and outcomes, rerun complete downstream nested fitting; diagnostic not conditional-null p-value
limitations: Only25 older stroke subjects, selected for compatible input; no general older adult clinical claim
Synthetic projection bypasses real pose estimation/occlusion
3D vs2D have different feature counts; comparison is diagnostic, not isolated causal projection effect
GDI toe mapping and source timebase uncertainties remain
Upstream auxiliary sample33 is small; negative C does not establish absence of useful deviation information
runtime: CPU only; no GPU jobs or monitoring automation
